title: Album Cover Similarity & Color Distance
text:
This analysis measures how similar album covers are across Taylor Swift and 21 popular artists based on their color concept and visual palettes.
Each album cover was analyzed across five core color dimensions:

Mean RGB (Red, Green, Blue channels normalized 0 to 1)
Brightness (perceptual luminance: \(0.299R + 0.587G + 0.114B\))
Saturation (chroma / vividness of colors)
Color Concept (e.g., Dark & Moody, Soft & Pastel, Cool & Blue, Warm & Red/Orange)

The Euclidean color distance measures similarity in this 5D color space:
\[d = \sqrt{\sum_{k} (x_{1,k} - x_{2,k})^2}\]
Smaller distances indicate album covers with closer color aesthetics and moods.

library(tidyverse)

features <- read_csv("../distance/album_color_features.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
closest <- read_csv("../distance/taylor_closest_matches.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

title: Album Cover Similarity & Color Distance
text:
Color Space: Brightness vs. Saturation
The scatter plot below displays where each album cover falls in the color space:

ggplot(features, aes(x = brightness, y = saturation, color = color_concept)) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = (artist == "Taylor Swift")), size = 3.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    name = "Artist",
    values = c("TRUE" = 17, "FALSE" = 16),
    labels = c("TRUE" = "Taylor Swift", "FALSE" = "Other Artists")
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  labs(
    title = "Album Covers in Color Space",
    subtitle = "Comparing Taylor Swift covers with 21 popular artists",
    x = "Mean Brightness (0 = Dark, 1 = Light)",
    y = "Mean Saturation (0 = Grayscale, 1 = Vivid)",
    color = "Color Concept"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
